FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 23 March 1990, after the draft 
finalized by the Sugar Industry Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture 
Division Council. 

Industrial screens are used by the sugar industry to grade sugar into the three grain sizes X', 'M' and 'S' 
which are prescribed in IS 498 : 1985 'Grading for vacuum pan sugar ( plantation white ) {fourth revision ) ' . 
They are also required for iJOi?/and dry seed separation. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final 
value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance 
with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revisea)\ The number of significant places 
retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



IS 12935 : 1990 



Indian Standard 



RECOMMENDED INDUSTRIAL SCREENS FOR 
GRADING SUGAR — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 Specifies material, dimensions and other 
requirements for industrial screens used in the 
sugar industry for grading sugar in accordance 
with IS 498 : 1985. 

2 REFERENCES 

2.1 The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard: 

IS No. Title

( plantation white ) 
{fourth revision )

sieves {first revision )

wire

3 MATERIAL 

3.1 Stainless steel wire — conforming to grade 
04Crl8NilO of IS 6528 : 1972 shall be used. 

4 DEMENSIONS 

4.1 A 4-deck system of screens is usually used for 
grading sugar. The four screens used are one 
each for L, M and S grades and fourth for either 
RORI separation or for dry seed separation. 

4.2 The dimensions for industrial screens for 
grading sugar shall be selected for those given in 
Table 1. 

4.2.1 Table 1 gives 12 aperture sizes and the 
corresponding wire diameters for both heavy and 
medium heavy wir^s which conform to the require- 
ments prescribed in IS 2405 (Part 1) : 1980. 

4.2.2 Heavy wires are recommended for screens 
with a capacity of more than 10 tons and mediiun 
heavy wires for screens with a capacity of less 
than 10 tons. 



5 MARKING 

5.1 The following particulars shall be marked on 
the screen: 

a) Indication of the source of manufacture, 

b) Batch or code number, 

c) Aperture size and, 

d) Wire diameter. 

5.2 The screens may also be marked with Standard 
Mark, details of which may be obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 



to between the purchaser and 



6 PACKING 

6.1 As agreed 
the supplier. 

7 SAMPLING 

7.1 As agreed to between the purchaser and 
the supplier. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standard Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any from without the prior permission in writing cf BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the 
course of implementing the standard, cf necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type of grade 
designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Revision of Indian Standards 

Indian Standards are reviewed periodically and revised, when necessary and amendments, if any, are 
issued from time to time. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of 
the latest amendments or edition. Comments on this Indian Standard may be sent in BIS giving the 
following reference :
